ConsolePrincipal.Description: The Ops Console identity allowed to use the role (shown in the console).

Properties.Description: Used by Ops Console for this account. Delete this stack to disconnect.

Content.description: Ops Console: deploy or roll back one project via server/pipeline.sh

runCommand: # OpsConsole-Deploy: deploy or roll back ONE project with the existing pipeline (server/pipeline.sh).
# Runs as root via SSM; the pipeline itself runs as ec2-user, exactly like a CI or manual deploy
# (same lock, pre-deploy DB backup, migrations, health check and auto-rollback).
# SSM substitutes the double-brace parameters below textually. Each one is limited by an allowedPattern in the
# document AND re-checked here, and none can contain quotes, spaces or shell metacharacters.
# Output: the pipeline log without colour codes (last 20 KB). Exit code: the pipeline's.
case "$ACTION" in deploy|rollback) ;; *) fail "unknown action" ;; esac
if [[ "$ACTION" == rollback && -n "$REF" && ! "$REF" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ ]]; then fail "rollback takes a commit sha"; fi
# Apps cloned over HTTPS from a GitHub App repo: the console leaves a short-lived, repo-scoped token in SSM
# (/ops-console/git-tokens/<project>). It is written to a 0600 file and handed to git through GIT_ASKPASS:

if tok="$(aws ssm get-parameter --region "$REGION" --name "/ops-console/git-tokens/$PROJECT" --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value --output text 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$tok" && "$tok" != None ]]; then
printf '#!/bin/sh\ncase "$1" in Username*) echo x-access-token ;; *) cat "$OPS_GIT_TOKEN_FILE" ;; esac\n' > "$TOKDIR/askpass.sh"
runuser -u ec2-user -- env -i HOME=/home/ec2-user USER=ec2-user LOGNAME=ec2-user LANG=C.UTF-8 \

Content.description: Ops Console: run a backup, restore-test a dump into a throwaway DB, export one for download, or manage off-site copies

Content.description: Ops Console: set up a new Node.js or Python app from a GitHub repository and deploy it (rolls back on failure)

runCommand: # OpsConsole-CreateApp: set up a NEW Node.js or Python app on this instance from a GitHub repository, then deploy it.
#   Python: the chosen version (installed from the OS repositories if missing), a virtual environment in
#   /opt/venvs/<project>, dependencies from requirements.txt or pyproject.toml, uvicorn (FastAPI) or gunicorn
#   (Flask, Django) started on the app's module, migrations with Alembic or manage.py migrate.
#   clone (as ec2-user, private repos through a short-lived token the console leaves in SSM) → pick a free port →

# project conf in /opt/deploy-state/projects (survives deploy.sh's rsync) → SSM /apps/

/{PORT,NODE_ENV}
#   → optional Postgres role + database (password generated here, DATABASE_URL straight to SSM)

# → systemd unit → nginx vhost → HTTPS (certbot) once DNS points here → pipeline.sh deploy

.
# Anything that fails rolls back everything this run created. Refuses if the project, unit, folder or vhost exists.
# Every parameter is pinned by allowedPattern in the document and re-checked here.
# Output: the run log (colour-free, last 20 KB) and a final JSON summary line. Secrets are never printed.
CREATED=()          # what to undo on failure, in order

python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; ok=sys.argv[1]=="true"; print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, "step": sys.argv[2], "error": sys.argv[3] or None, "port": int(sys.argv[4]) if sys.argv[4] else None, "tls": sys.argv[5]=="true", "database": sys.argv[6] or None, "domain": sys.argv[7]}))' \
log "rolling back what this run created"

unit)   systemctl disable --now "$PROJECT" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "/etc/systemd/system/$PROJECT.service"; rm -rf "/etc/systemd/system/app-secrets@$PROJECT.service.d"; rm -f "/run/app-secrets/$PROJECT.env"; systemctl daemon-reload ;;
vhost)  rm -f "/etc/nginx/conf.d/$PROJECT.conf"; nginx -t 2>/dev/null && systemctl reload nginx ;;
db)     printf 'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "%s" WITH (FORCE);\nDROP ROLE IF EXISTS "%s";\n' "$DBNAME" "$DBROLE" | pgsu >/dev/null 2>&1 ;;
ssm)    for k in PORT NODE_ENV DATABASE_URL; do aws ssm delete-parameter --region "$REGION" --name "/apps/$PROJECT/$k" 2>/dev/null; done ;;
conf)   rm -f "$STATE_PROJ/$PROJECT.conf"; rm -rf "/opt/deploy-state/$PROJECT" ;;   # the pipeline's history/backups dir for this new app
fail() { log "✘ $*"; undo; summary false "$*"; exit 1; }
pgsu() { runuser -u ec2-user -- env -i HOME=/home/ec2-user PATH=/usr/bin:/bin psql -X -q -h localhost -U postgres -w -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1; }

m = re.search(r":(\d+)\s", line.split()[3] + " ") if len(line.split()) > 3 else None
print(next(p for p in range(5000, 6000) if p not in used))

printf '#!/bin/sh\ncase "$1" in Username*) echo x-access-token ;; *) cat "$OPS_GIT_TOKEN_FILE" ;; esac\n' > "$TOKDIR/askpass.sh"
asec2 git clone --quiet --branch "$BRANCH" "https://github.com/$REPO.git" "/opt/apps/$PROJECT" || fail "git clone failed (does the GitHub App have access to $REPO?)"
[[ -f "$APPDIR/requirements.txt" || -f "$APPDIR/pyproject.toml" ]] || fail "no requirements.txt or pyproject.toml in ${SUBDIR:-the repository root}"
[[ "$FRAMEWORK" != django || -f "$APPDIR/manage.py" ]] || fail "no manage.py in ${SUBDIR:-the repository root} (Django)"
dnf -y -q install "python$PYVER" "python$PYVER-pip" >/tmp/opscreate-dnf.log 2>&1 || { tail -3 /tmp/opscreate-dnf.log; fail "could not install Python $PYVER"; }
asec2 "/usr/bin/python$PYVER" -m venv "$VENV" || fail "could not create the virtual environment"

DBNAME=""; fail "a database or role for $PROJECT already exists"
PW="$(python3 -I -c 'import secrets; print("".join(c if c.isalnum() else "x" for c in secrets.token_urlsafe(32)))')"
"$DBROLE" "$PW" "$DBNAME" "$DBROLE" "$DBNAME" "$DBNAME" "$DBROLE" | pgsu >/dev/null || fail "could not create the database"
python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"Name": sys.argv[1], "Value": sys.argv[2], "Type": "SecureString", "Overwrite": True}))' \
| aws ssm put-parameter --region "$REGION" --cli-input-json file:///dev/stdin >/dev/null || fail "could not save DATABASE_URL"
aws ssm put-parameter --region "$REGION" --name "/apps/$PROJECT/PORT" --type String --value "$PORT" --overwrite >/dev/null || fail "could not save PORT"
aws ssm put-parameter --region "$REGION" --name "/apps/$PROJECT/NODE_ENV" --type String --value production --overwrite >/dev/null || fail "could not save NODE_ENV"
# dependencies on every deploy (a rollback installs the old commit's); the server package is added if the app doesn't list it
if [[ "$FRAMEWORK" == fastapi ]]; then SRV=uvicorn; SRVPKG="'uvicorn[standard]'"; else SRV=gunicorn; SRVPKG=gunicorn; fi
if [[ -f "$APPDIR/requirements.txt" ]]; then DEPS="$VENV/bin/pip install $PIPQ -r requirements.txt"; else DEPS="$VENV/bin/pip install $PIPQ ."; fi
BUILDC="$([[ "$BUILD" == yes && "$FRAMEWORK" == django ]] && echo "$VENV/bin/python manage.py collectstatic --noinput")"
# Created by the Ops Console (OpsConsole-CreateApp) for $REPO; kept in the state dir so deploy.sh never removes it.
# two worker processes; only this server talks to the app (nginx in front), so trust its forwarded headers only
# Created by the Ops Console for $REPO. Secrets: SSM /apps/$PROJECT/* loaded by app-secrets@$PROJECT.
# the secrets loader defaults to af-south-1: pin this instance's region for this app
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --quiet "$PROJECT" || fail "could not install the systemd unit"
# load /apps/$PROJECT/* now: the first deploy's migrations read DATABASE_* from it, and it proves SSM access works
systemctl restart "app-secrets@$PROJECT" || fail "could not load the app's settings from SSM (instance role permissions in $REGION?)"
# Created by the Ops Console for $REPO
nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx || fail "nginx rejected the new site"
# The console already waited for Route 53 to report the record live; this instance's resolver may still hold an old
# "no such name" answer for a few minutes. Let's Encrypt checks public DNS, so try the certificate either way.
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do [[ "$(getent hosts "$DOMAIN" | awk '{print $1}' | head -1)" == "$MYIP" ]] && { resolved=true; break; }; sleep 5; done
$resolved || log "this instance doesn't resolve $DOMAIN yet (DNS cache); trying the certificate anyway"
if certbot --nginx -d "$DOMAIN" --non-interactive --agree-tos --redirect --register-unsafely-without-email; then TLS=true; log "HTTPS certificate issued for $DOMAIN"
else log "⚠ certbot failed; the app is reachable over HTTP only for now (re-run: sudo certbot --nginx -d $DOMAIN)"; fi
asec2 DEPLOY_ACTOR="$ACTOR" DEPLOY_TRIGGER=ops-console bash /opt/deploy/server/pipeline.sh deploy "$PROJECT" "$BRANCH" </dev/null || fail "the first deploy failed (see the pipeline output above)"
log "✔ $PROJECT is live at http$([[ $TLS == true ]] && echo s)://$DOMAIN"

Content.description: Ops Console: add or remove one public key of a login user (never root; keeps ec2-user's last key)

runCommand: # OpsConsole-SshKeys: add or remove one public key in a login user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.
#   action=add    user=<login user> key=<one public key line>
#   Temporary laptop access (temporary=yes): add puts the key in with from="<sources>",expiry-time="<local time>"
#   (sshd refuses it after that even if nothing removes it); a key that is already there without expiry-time is
#   left alone (added=false). remove with temporary=yes only ever removes lines that carry an expiry-time.
# Only normal login users (uid >= 1000, a login shell and a home): never root. Refuses to remove ec2-user's last
# key (SSH lock-out). Keeps a copy of the previous file as authorized_keys.ops-console.bak.
case "$ACTION" in add|remove) ;; *) echo '{"ok":false,"error":"unknown action"}'; exit 2 ;; esac
import ipaddress, json, os, pwd, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time
action, user, key, fp, sources, expires, temporary = sys.argv[1:8]
print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, "action": action, "user": user, **kw})); sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
done(False, error=f"there is no user {user} on this instance")
if pw.pw_uid < 1000 or pw.pw_shell.endswith(("nologin", "false")) or not os.path.isdir(pw.pw_dir):
done(False, error=f"{user} is not a normal login user")
if p in TYPES and i + 1 < len(parts):
r = subprocess.run(["ssh-keygen", "-lf", "-"], input=f"{p} {parts[i + 1]}\n", capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
return m.group(1) if m else None
keyed = [(l, fingerprint_of(l)) for l in lines]
count = sum(1 for _, f in keyed if f)
is_temp = lambda l: "expiry-time=" in l.split(" ssh-")[0].split(" ecdsa-")[0].split(" sk-")[0]
if not KEY_RE.match(key): done(False, error="that doesn't look like a single OpenSSH public key line")
if not new_fp: done(False, error="ssh-keygen could not read that key")
srcs = [str(ipaddress.ip_network(x, strict=True)) for x in sources.split(",") if x]
if not srcs or not expires: done(False, error="temporary keys need a source and an expiry")
if int(expires) <= time.time() or int(expires) > time.time() + 12 * 3600: done(False, error="invalid expiry")
if any(f == new_fp and not is_temp(l) for l, f in keyed):
done(True, fingerprint=new_fp, added=False, permanent=True, keys=count)   # already has permanent access: leave it
# sshd reads expiry-time in the instance's local time zone
keep = [l for l, f in keyed if f != new_fp]
done(True, fingerprint=new_fp, added=True, permanent=False, keys=len([1 for _, f in keyed if f and f != new_fp]) + 1, expiresLocal=stamp)
if not FP_RE.match(fp): done(False, error="invalid fingerprint")
keep = [l for l, f in keyed if not (f == fp and is_temp(l))]
if len(keep) == len(lines): done(True, fingerprint=fp, removed=0, keys=count)   # already gone (or never temporary)
done(True, fingerprint=fp, removed=len(lines) - len(keep), keys=count - (len(lines) - len(keep)))
if not KEY_RE.match(key): done(False, error="that doesn't look like a single OpenSSH public key line")
if not new_fp: done(False, error="ssh-keygen could not read that key")
if any(f == new_fp for _, f in keyed): done(False, error=f"{user} already has this key", fingerprint=new_fp)
if not FP_RE.match(fp): done(False, error="invalid fingerprint")
keep = [l for l, f in keyed if f != fp]
if len(keep) == len(lines): done(False, error=f"{user} has no key with fingerprint {fp}")
done(False, error="that is ec2-user's last key: removing it would lock everyone out of SSH. Add another key first.")

Content.description: Ops Console: install what the console needs on a fresh Amazon Linux 2023 server (safe to re-run)

runCommand: # OpsConsole-PrepareServer: turn a fresh Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance into one the console can run apps on.
# Safe to run again (every step checks first). Installs:
#   nginx, git, certbot, Node.js (newest of 22/20/18 available), PostgreSQL 15 (password auth on localhost, a
#   generated postgres password in ~/.pgpass for ec2-user and root), a swap file on small instances,
#   the console's server files from a release bundle (pipeline, settings loader, status agent, backups) into
#   /opt/deploy, the read-only status agent (127.0.0.1:9100) and the nightly database backup timer.
# Parameters: bundleUrl (our public release bundle) + sha256 (checked before anything is unpacked).
# The status agent's database password is read from SSM /apps/ops-dashboard/PGPASSWORD (the console puts it there).
# Output: progress lines, then one JSON line {"ok":…,"step":…,"error":…,"node":…,"steps":[…]}.

emit() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; ok=sys.argv[1]=="1"; print(json.dumps({"ok":ok,"step":sys.argv[2],"error":sys.argv[3] or None,"node":sys.argv[4] or None,"steps":[s for s in sys.argv[5:] if s]}))' "$@"; }
[[ "${ID:-}" == amzn && "${VERSION_ID:-}" == 2023* ]] || fail "only Amazon Linux 2023 is supported for now (this is ${PRETTY_NAME:-unknown})"

REGION="$(TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -m 2 -X PUT http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -H 'X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 60') && curl -fsS -m 2 -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/placement/region)" || fail "could not read the instance region"
(( FREE_GB >= 2 )) || fail "only ${FREE_GB} GB free on / (need at least 2 GB)"
log "Amazon Linux 2023 in $REGION, ${MEM_MB} MB memory, ${FREE_GB} GB free"
for v in 22 20 18; do dnf -q list --available "nodejs$v" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { NODEPKG="nodejs$v nodejs$v-npm"; break; }; done
dnf -y -q install nginx git certbot python3-certbot-nginx postgresql15-server postgresql15 $NODEPKG >/tmp/opsprep-dnf.log 2>&1 || { tail -5 /tmp/opsprep-dnf.log; fail "package install failed"; }
# versioned Node packages install /usr/bin/node-NN: make sure plain `node` / `npm` exist
NODEV="$(node -v 2>/dev/null)" || fail "node is not on the PATH after installing $NODEPKG"
if fallocate -l 1G /swapfile && chmod 600 /swapfile && mkswap -q /swapfile && swapon /swapfile; then
did "1 GB swap file (small instance: keeps npm builds from running out of memory)"
rm -f /swapfile; log "⚠ could not add a swap file; continuing without one"
systemctl enable --quiet --now postgresql || fail "postgresql did not start"
sudo -u postgres psql -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "ALTER ROLE postgres WITH PASSWORD '$PGPW'" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the postgres password"
# password (md5) for TCP and local socket logins; keep peer for replication as shipped
psql -X -q -h localhost -U postgres -w -d postgres -c 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null || fail "cannot log in to PostgreSQL with the generated password"
# system logs: keep at most 200 MB on the server (older days are copied to the backup bucket with the off-site copies)
curl -fsS -m 120 -o "$TMP/bundle.tgz" "$BUNDLE_URL" || fail "could not download the release bundle"
echo "$BUNDLE_SHA  $TMP/bundle.tgz" | sha256sum -c --status || fail "the release bundle's checksum does not match"
mkdir -p "$TMP/x" && tar -xzf "$TMP/bundle.tgz" -C "$TMP/x" --no-same-owner || fail "could not unpack the bundle"
for d in server systemd ops-dashboard templates; do [[ -d "$TMP/x/$d" ]] || fail "bundle is missing $d/"; done
for d in server systemd ops-dashboard templates; do rm -rf "/opt/deploy/$d"; cp -a "$TMP/x/$d" "/opt/deploy/$d"; done
did "server files (pipeline, settings loader, status agent, backups) in /opt/deploy"
|| fail "missing SSM /apps/ops-dashboard/PGPASSWORD (the console sets it before preparing)"
psql -X -q -h localhost -U postgres -w -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 >/dev/null <<SQL || fail "could not create the read-only monitoring role"
DO \$\$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'ops_monitor') THEN CREATE ROLE ops_monitor LOGIN; END IF; END \$\$;
ALTER ROLE ops_monitor WITH LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE PASSWORD '$MPW' CONNECTION LIMIT 5;
systemctl enable --quiet ops-dashboard && systemctl restart ops-dashboard || fail "the status agent did not start"
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:9100/healthz >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
curl -fsS -m 2 http://127.0.0.1:9100/healthz >/dev/null || { journalctl -u ops-dashboard -n 15 --no-pager; fail "the status agent is not answering"; }
systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable --quiet --now db-backup.timer || fail "could not enable the backup timer"
did "nightly database backups (kept 14 days on this server)"
systemctl enable --quiet --now nginx || fail "nginx did not start"
nginx -t >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "the nginx configuration test failed"

Content.description: Ops Console: issue the HTTPS certificate of one console-created app once its domain points at this server

runCommand: # OpsConsole-EnableHttps: issue the Let's Encrypt certificate for ONE app created by the console, once its domain
# points at this server (DNS kept at another provider: the customer adds the A record after the app is created).
# Reads the domain from the app's own conf (never from the caller), checks public DNS first, then runs certbot --nginx.
# Safe to re-run: an existing certificate is reported, not replaced.

out() { python3 -I -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"ok": sys.argv[1] == "1", "tls": sys.argv[2] == "1", "domain": sys.argv[3], "resolves": [x for x in sys.argv[4].split(",") if x], "expected": sys.argv[5], "reason": sys.argv[6]}))' "$@"; }
[[ -f "$CONF" ]] || fail "$PROJECT was not created by the console (no $CONF)"
[[ "$MYIP" =~ ^[0-9.]+$ ]] || fail "this server has no public IPv4 address"
if [[ -d "/etc/letsencrypt/live/$DOMAIN" ]]; then out 1 1 "$DOMAIN" "" "$MYIP" "HTTPS is already enabled."; exit 0; fi
# public DNS as Let's Encrypt will see it (not this server's cache): ask a public resolver over HTTPS
try: print(",".join(a["data"] for a in json.load(sys.stdin).get("Answer", []) if a.get("type") == 1))
if [[ -z "$RESOLVES" ]]; then out 0 0 "$DOMAIN" "" "$MYIP" "$DOMAIN has no A record yet. Add one pointing at $MYIP, wait a few minutes, then check again."; exit 0; fi
out 0 0 "$DOMAIN" "$RESOLVES" "$MYIP" "$DOMAIN points at $RESOLVES. Change its A record to $MYIP only, wait a few minutes, then check again."; exit 0
out 0 0 "$DOMAIN" "$RESOLVES" "$MYIP" "Let's Encrypt refused the certificate: $(grep -m1 -iE 'detail|error' /tmp/opshttps.log | cut -c1-200 | tr -d '"\\')"

Content.description: Ops Console: list, install, start, stop or remove server components (PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Valkey, SQLite, Python) from the OS repositories

runCommand: # OpsConsole-Components: what runs on the server besides the apps, and installing/starting/stopping/removing it.
# Amazon Linux 2023 packages only (no third-party repositories); versions offered are whatever the OS repositories have.
#   list                         installed components, versions, running state, memory, and what can be installed
#   install <component> [ver]    postgresql (one version per server), mariadb, valkey, sqlite, python (several versions)
#   start|stop <component>       postgresql, mariadb, valkey (PostgreSQL is never stopped on the console's own server)
#   remove <component> [ver]     valkey, sqlite, python <ver>, mariadb (only without databases of its own);
#                                never PostgreSQL; data folders are always kept
# Databases and Valkey listen on the server only (127.0.0.1). Installs check free memory first.
# Output: progress lines, then one JSON line {"ok":…,"action":…,"component":…,"error":…,"components":[…],"host":{…}}.

need_mb() { local need=$1 have; have="$(mem_avail_mb)"; (( have >= need )) || { fail "needs about ${need} MB of free memory and the server has ${have} MB: stop something first or use a larger instance"; return 1; }; }
need_disk() { local gb=$(( $(df --output=avail -k / | tail -1) / 1048576 )); (( gb >= 1 )) || { fail "less than 1 GB free on the disk"; return 1; }; }

fail "only Amazon Linux 2023 is supported for now (this is ${PRETTY_NAME:-unknown})"
if [[ -n "$cur" ]]; then fail "PostgreSQL ${cur//[^0-9]/} is already installed (one version per server)"
v="${VERSION:-}"; [[ -n "$v" ]] || for c in 17 16 15; do available "postgresql$c-server" && { v=$c; break; }; done
[[ "$v" =~ ^1[5-9]$ ]] && available "postgresql$v-server" || fail "PostgreSQL ${v:-?} is not offered by this OS"
systemctl enable --quiet --now postgresql || fail "postgresql did not start"
# the same login setup as Prepare server: a generated postgres password in ~/.pgpass, password logins on localhost
sudo -u postgres psql -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "ALTER ROLE postgres WITH PASSWORD '$PGPW'" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the postgres password"
if rpm -qa --qf '%{NAME}\n' | grep -qE '^mariadb[0-9]+-server$'; then log "MariaDB is already installed"
pkg=""; for c in 1011 105; do [[ -n "$VERSION" && "$VERSION" != "${c:0:2}.${c:2}" ]] && continue; available "mariadb$c-server" && { pkg="mariadb$c-server"; break; }; done
[[ -n "$pkg" ]] || fail "MariaDB ${VERSION:-} is not offered by this OS"
if (( MEM_MB < 2048 )); then echo '# small server: keep memory low'; echo 'innodb_buffer_pool_size = 64M'; echo 'performance_schema = OFF'; echo 'max_connections = 40'; fi
systemctl enable --quiet --now mariadb || fail "mariadb did not start"
# root logs in through the server's socket only (MariaDB's default); remove the anonymous users and the test database
mariadb -e "DELETE FROM mysql.global_priv WHERE User=''; DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS test; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;" >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "⚠ could not tidy the default users"
if installed valkey; then log "Valkey is already installed"
systemctl enable --quiet --now valkey || fail "valkey did not start"
[[ -z "$ERR" ]] && log "✔ Valkey on 127.0.0.1:6379 (up to ${CAP} MB, refuses new writes when full)"
installed sqlite && log "SQLite is already installed" || { dnf_install sqlite && log "✔ SQLite (the command-line tool, used for backups)"; } ;;
if installed "python$VERSION"; then log "Python $VERSION is already installed"
else available "python$VERSION" || fail "Python $VERSION is not offered by this OS"
[[ -z "$ERR" ]] && dnf_install "python$VERSION" "python$VERSION-pip" && log "✔ Python $VERSION (python$VERSION; apps get their own virtual environments)"
postgresql) unit=postgresql; [[ -n "$(pg_pkg)" ]] || fail "PostgreSQL is not installed" ;;
mariadb) unit=mariadb; rpm -qa --qf '%{NAME}\n' | grep -qE '^mariadb[0-9]+-server$' || fail "MariaDB is not installed" ;;
valkey) unit=valkey; installed valkey || fail "Valkey is not installed" ;;
*) fail "$COMPONENT has nothing to start or stop" ;;
fail "the Ops Console runs on this server and keeps its own data in PostgreSQL: it can't be stopped here"
if [[ "$ACTION" == start ]]; then systemctl enable --quiet --now "$unit" || fail "$unit did not start"
else systemctl disable --quiet --now "$unit" || fail "$unit did not stop"; fi
postgresql) fail "PostgreSQL is not removed from the console: it holds the apps' data (and backups depend on it)" ;;
if [[ -z "$pkg" ]]; then log "MariaDB is not installed"
own="$(mariadb -N -e "SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name NOT IN ('mysql','information_schema','performance_schema','sys')" 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
if [[ "$own" != 0 ]]; then fail "MariaDB still has ${own} database(s): it is only removed when it holds none"
else systemctl disable --quiet --now mariadb 2>/dev/null; dnf -y -q remove "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "could not remove $pkg"
[[ -z "$ERR" ]] && log "✔ MariaDB removed (its data folder /var/lib/mysql is kept)"

valkey) systemctl disable --quiet --now valkey 2>/dev/null; installed valkey && { dnf -y -q remove valkey >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "could not remove valkey"; }; [[ -z "$ERR" ]] && log "✔ Valkey removed (/var/lib/valkey is kept)" ;;
sqlite) installed sqlite && { dnf -y -q remove sqlite >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "could not remove sqlite"; }; [[ -z "$ERR" ]] && log "✔ SQLite tool removed (database files are kept)" ;;
[[ "$VERSION" =~ ^3\.1[0-9]$ ]] || fail "choose the Python version to remove"
installed "python$VERSION" && { dnf -y -q remove "python$VERSION" "python$VERSION-pip" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "could not remove python$VERSION"; }
action, component, err = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
try: return subprocess.run(a, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60).stdout.strip()

'active': active('valkey') if 'valkey' in rpms else None, 'memoryMb': mem('valkey-server') if 'valkey' in rpms else 0, 'needMb': 64, 'service': 'valkey',

print(json.dumps({'ok': not err, 'action': action, 'component': component or None, 'error': err or None, 'components': comps, 'host': host}))
